fields.description:
## Context / Problem

The graph loader/BFS centralization (985c-32d2-e828-4e6a, Gerrit 1708, merged 1c3e945cb8)
named two behaviours as explicit helpers that had previously been inline, and the rebar
code-review bot flagged both as untested. The gaps are PRE-EXISTING — the same logic was
uncovered while inline — but naming them made them visible. Nothing regresses today; the
risk is that a future traversal or loader refactor silently drops either behaviour with the
suite still green.

## Approach

Characterization tests ONLY — no `src/rebar` change. Follow the pattern of
`test_get_all_blocked_by_accumulates_targets_without_a_ticket_dir` (added by 985c in
`tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_cycles.py`): assert the behaviour that exists today so the
tests pin the contract rather than propose a new one. Each new test was validated by
mutating the production branch locally, observing the test go red, and reverting — the
mutation results are recorded per criterion below.

### Gap 1 — the cross-level traversal refusal (`rebar.graph._graph`)

`_is_at_level` is called twice: once inside `_same_level_neighbors`'s `neighbors` closure as
the CURRENT-side guard (a node of another type is not expanded), and once as the TARGET-side
guard on each candidate dep (`if target and target not in visited and _is_at_level(...)`).
Every existing `check_cycle_at_level` test in `test_graph_cycles.py` uses a single uniform
level, so the target-side guard is never exercised.

The two guards are not interchangeable, and this dictates the test shape: for an
`epic → task → epic` chain the CURRENT-side guard alone already stops the walk, so deleting
the target-side call leaves that case still returning False. The only mutation-sensitive
probe is a DIRECT cross-level edge whose far end IS the queried `source_id`:
`check_cycle_at_level("task-M", "epic-B", level="epic")` where `epic-B depends_on task-M`.
Today `bfs` (in `rebar.graph._relations`) accumulates nothing, so the answer is False;
with the target-side `_is_at_level` deleted, `task-M` is yielded and accumulated and the
answer flips to True. Both shapes get a test: the direct one pins the guard, the
`epic → task → epic` hop one pins the end-to-end "a lower-level hop cannot reconnect two
same-level nodes" contract.

### Gap 2 — the three tombstone-loader branches (`rebar.graph._unblock`)

All three are driven through the public `detect_newly_unblocked`, not the private
`_load_states_with_tombstones`. One shared fixture shape makes each branch observable: a
target ticket carrying two `depends_on` LINK events (so the blocking edges live in the
TARGET's dir and survive an unreducible blocker dir), one blocker closed by the batch and one
blocker tombstoned. `_was_already_unblocked` then cannot short-circuit, so the verdict turns
entirely on how the tombstoned blocker's status is loaded.

- (a) reduce-returns-None + tombstone present yields a status-only stub. Observable only when
  the recorded status is NON-terminal: with the stub the blocker reads `open` and the target
  is NOT newly unblocked; without it the blocker is absent and
  `_is_closed_after_batch`'s "missing dir → tombstoned, treat as closed" fallback unblocks
  the target. The test therefore uses a tombstone recording `open` — `_read_tombstone_status`
  takes `.get("status", "deleted")` verbatim with no validation, and that verbatim
  propagation is exactly what the test pins.
- (b) a present tombstone's status OVERRIDES the reduced status: an `open` blocker dir with a
  `{"status": "deleted"}` tombstone (the payload `rebar._commands.delete` writes) counts as
  closed and unblocks the target.
- (c) a malformed tombstone degrades to `deleted` rather than to "no tombstone": the same
  `open` blocker dir with unparseable tombstone bytes still counts as closed.

## Scope

- `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_cycles.py` — two tests for the level-confined traversal,
  reusing the existing `_helpers._make_ticket` / `_write_link_event` / `_get_check_cycle_at_level`.
- `tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py` — three tests, reusing the file's existing
  `_write_ticket` and `_write_depends_on_link` helpers. No new helper: `_write_ticket(deps=...)`
  is unusable here because it writes `blocks` links into the BLOCKER's dir, which an
  unreducible blocker dir cannot carry, but `_write_depends_on_link` already writes the LINK
  into the DEPENDENT's dir — exactly the shape these fixtures need.

No file under `src/rebar` is modified. If a test reveals a real defect, it is recorded and
filed as a `discovered_from` bug rather than fixed here.

## Testing

The new tests ARE the deliverable; each is validated by mutation rather than by assertion of
a guess:

- delete the target-side `_is_at_level(...)` from `_same_level_neighbors` → the direct
  cross-level test goes red (verified: verdict flips False → True).
- delete the `state is None` + tombstone stub branch → test (a) goes red (verified: `[]` →
  `['tkt-target']`).
- delete the `state["status"] = tombstone_status` override → test (b) goes red (verified:
  `['tkt-target']` → `[]`).
- make `_read_tombstone_status`'s `except` return `None` instead of `"deleted"` → test (c)
  goes red (verified: `['tkt-target']` → `[]`).

Edge/negative coverage inside the new tests: an unreducible ticket dir, unparseable tombstone
bytes, and a cross-level dep that must NOT be traversed. No new production behaviour, so
there is no happy path beyond the existing suite, which must stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_cycles.py` contains a test asserting
      `check_cycle_at_level("task-M", "epic-B", "epic", tracker) is False` for an
      `epic-B depends_on task-M` tracker; checked by deleting the target-side `_is_at_level`
      call and observing that exact test fail, then reverting.
- [ ] `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_cycles.py` contains a test asserting
      `check_cycle_at_level("epic-A", "epic-B", "epic", tracker) is False` for an
      `epic-B depends_on task-M depends_on epic-A` chain, so a lower-level hop cannot
      reconnect two same-level nodes; checked by running that test against the unmodified
      tree and seeing it pass.
- [ ] `tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py` contains a test that fails when the
      `state is None` + tombstone-present stub branch of `_load_states_with_tombstones` is
      deleted; checked by that deletion + `pytest` on the single test, then reverting.
- [ ] `tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py` contains a test that fails when the
      `state["status"] = tombstone_status` override is deleted; checked the same way.
- [ ] `tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py` contains a test that fails when
      `_read_tombstone_status`'s exception handler stops returning `"deleted"`; checked the
      same way.
- [ ] `git diff --name-only origin/main` lists only the two test files — no `src/rebar` path.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0, and
      `pytest tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_cycles.py tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py`
      is green.
